name: Linguacapades
about: Linguacapades maps where you stand on language: who sets its rules, what your dialect says about you, whether your words shape your thoughts, and what is happening to the world's tongues. Positions everyone holds and almost no one has ever stated — until they compare maps.

categories.name: Rules & standards
categories.about: How correctness, dictionaries, and linguistic evolution should be treated.

hovertip.issue: Are grammar rules timeless guardrails against decay, or merely snapshots of how prestige groups happen to speak?

poles.label: Classical Standard Care
text: Classical Standard Care
Shared grammar standards preserve precision across centuries and keep prose from dissolving into ambiguity.

poles.label: Contextual Register Mastery
text: Contextual Register Mastery
Formal standards and street slang are both valid tools; real fluency means knowing which fits the room.

poles.label: Pure Usage Descriptivism
text: Pure Usage Descriptivism
Living languages are governed by native speakers' brains, never by style-guide scolds.

hovertip.issue: When a usage is disputed, whose ruling settles it?

poles.label: Dictionaries & academies
poles.text: Institutions exist to keep the record: dictionaries and academies codify the standard so strangers can rely on it.

poles.label: Educated usage
poles.text: Correctness is what careful, educated speakers and writers actually do — the standard lives in practice, not in a rulebook.

poles.label: Every speaker
poles.text: A language belongs to everyone who speaks it; if a community understands it, it is correct there.

hovertip.issue: How should children learn their own language's grammar?

poles.label: Teach the rules
poles.text: Explicit rules give every child access to the standard dialect — and with it, to exams, jobs, and institutions.

poles.label: Teach the ear
poles.text: Children absorb grammar by reading and speaking; drilled rules mostly teach them to fear their own voice.

hovertip.issue: Should irregular spelling systems be preserved for historical depth, or reformed to match actual pronunciation?

poles.label: Etymological Historical Spelling
text: Etymological Historical Spelling
Traditional spelling links readers effortlessly across dialects and preserves visible roots of meaning.

poles.label: Phonemic Simplification
text: Phonemic Simplification
Irregular orthography wastes years of childhood schooling and creates unnecessary literacy barriers.

hovertip.issue: Should a language freely absorb foreign words, or invent native equivalents to protect its character?

poles.label: Welcoming Lexical Borrowing
text: Welcoming Lexical Borrowing
Borrowing freely enriches expressive nuance and reflects living contact between cultures.

poles.label: Native Coining & Purism
text: Native Coining & Purism
Transparent native compounds keep vocabulary intelligible to ordinary speakers without elite foreign schooling.

categories.name: Dialect & identity
categories.about: How regional speech, class markers, and multilingualism shape belonging.

hovertip.issue: Should schools and media cultivate a uniform standard accent, or celebrate regional and ethnic dialects equally?

poles.label: Shared Neutral Broadcast Norm
text: Shared Neutral Broadcast Norm
A common standard dialect gives every child equal access to national institutions and wide intelligibility.

poles.label: Proud Vernacular Diversity
text: Proud Vernacular Diversity
Stigmatizing non-standard dialects penalizes working-class and minority speakers for how their families talk.

hovertip.issue: Is African American English a rule-governed variety in its own right?

poles.label: A full system
poles.text: It has its own consistent grammar — habitual 'be', copula deletion — as systematic as any variety on earth.

poles.label: The standard first
poles.text: Whatever its internal logic, children are graded against the standard; schools owe them the standard first.

hovertip.issue: Is mixing two languages mid-sentence (like Spanglish) a creative gift or a sign of eroding mastery in both?

poles.label: Keep Tongues Distinct
text: Keep Tongues Distinct
Mastering each language cleanly on its own terms preserves deep literary range and clarity.

poles.label: Fluid Translanguaging
text: Fluid Translanguaging
Bilingual brains naturally draw on their entire repertoire, creating expressive agility neither tongue has alone.

hovertip.issue: What does slang do to a language?

poles.label: The growing edge
poles.text: Slang is where the language grows — new words for new feelings, minted by the young and the marginal first.

poles.label: Noise
poles.text: Most slang is mayfly noise; the tiny fraction that survives did not need anyone's permission.

categories.name: Language & thought
categories.about: How language relates to cognition, human nature, and reality.

hovertip.issue: Does the specific language you speak subtly nudge your attention, or build a fundamentally different reality?

poles.label: Universal Mentalese
text: Universal Mentalese
All human beings share the same underlying conceptual toolkit and can express any thought in any tongue.

poles.label: Habitual Framing Effects
text: Habitual Framing Effects
Grammatical gender, color terms, and spatial frames measurably bias what speakers notice and remember.

poles.label: Deep Worldview Determinism
text: Deep Worldview Determinism
Each language encodes an irreducible metaphysics that cannot be fully translated into another.

hovertip.issue: Are children born with a specialized biological language faculty, or do they learn grammar via general pattern-finding?

poles.label: Innate Universal Grammar
text: Innate Universal Grammar
Children master intricate syntax from sparse input far too fast without built-in structural constraints.

poles.label: Cultural Usage-Based Learning
text: Cultural Usage-Based Learning
General social cognition, statistical learning, and communicative pressure explain grammar without mysterious innate modules.

hovertip.issue: What do words with no equivalent — saudade, hygge, Schadenfreude — show?

poles.label: Windows
poles.text: Each one is a window: a feeling a whole culture noticed and yours walked past.

poles.label: Party tricks
poles.text: Anything can be paraphrased; 'untranslatable' usually means 'takes a sentence instead of a word'.

hovertip.issue: Does speaking two languages change how a mind works?

poles.label: A different mind
poles.text: Two languages mean two categorizations of everything; bilinguals literally deliberate differently in each.

poles.label: Two toolkits
poles.text: It is two toolkits on one bench — handy, occasionally tangled, but the carpenter is the same.

categories.name: The world's tongues
categories.about: Language extinction, global English, and revitalization efforts.

hovertip.issue: As half the world's seven thousand languages face extinction this century, what does humanity owe them?

poles.label: Active Revitalization Funding
text: Active Revitalization Funding
Every living language holds irreplaceable ecological knowledge and human dignity worth reviving in schools.

poles.label: Digital Archival Preservation
text: Digital Archival Preservation
When communities shift voluntarily, recording rich grammars and stories honors heritage without forcing children.

poles.label: Natural Linguistic Darwinism
text: Natural Linguistic Darwinism
Languages have always merged and vanished as people seek wider connection; mourning is sentimental.

hovertip.issue: Should dead or dying languages be revived, as Hebrew was and Irish is attempted?

poles.label: Worth the cost
poles.text: Hebrew proves a language can come home; revival returns a people's voice to them.

poles.label: A loving fiction
poles.text: A revived language is a new language in old clothes — worth loving, but not the thing that was lost.

hovertip.issue: How should humanity bridge language barriers across science, trade, and diplomacy?

poles.label: Embrace Global English
text: Embrace Global English
A de facto shared second language unlocks global science and travel for billions right now.

poles.label: Artificial Neutral Auxiliary
text: Artificial Neutral Auxiliary
Constructed languages like Esperanto avoid handing unfair cultural dominance to native English speakers.

poles.label: Multilingual Machine Mediation
text: Multilingual Machine Mediation
Real-time neural translation lets everyone speak their mother tongue without forcing linguistic convergence.

hovertip.issue: Should immigrant families press children to keep the heritage language?

poles.label: Keep them alive
poles.text: The grandparents' tongue is the family's memory and the child's second world; losing it by the third generation is the usual, quiet grief.

poles.label: Let children choose
poles.text: Children gravitate to the language of their lives; forcing heritage fluency breeds resentment, not bilinguals.

hovertip.issue: Should immigrant and minority education prioritize rapid fluency in the dominant language, or sustained bilingual schooling?

poles.label: Rapid Majority-Language Immersion
text: Rapid Majority-Language Immersion
Early mastery of the shared civic language accelerates economic integration and social cohesion.

poles.label: Dual-Language Heritage Maintenance
text: Dual-Language Heritage Maintenance
Sustaining home languages strengthens family bonds, cognitive flexibility, and academic confidence.

hovertip.issue: Latin, Sanskrit, Classical Greek: why learn a language no one speaks?

poles.label: Worth learning
poles.text: They are keys to libraries nothing else opens, and grammar training no living language gives as cleanly.

poles.label: A beautiful luxury
poles.text: A beautiful luxury for those with leisure; the hours buy more world in a living tongue.

categories.name: Writing & script
categories.about: How writing systems carry identity, and what new media do to the written word.

hovertip.issue: Serbia's two alphabets, simplified and traditional characters: how much identity rides on the script itself?

poles.label: Script is identity
poles.text: A script is a flag you read with; communities defend theirs because changing it rewrites who the texts belong to.

hovertip.issue: What has texting done to writing?

poles.label: Ruining writing
poles.text: Informal habits bleed upward: punctuation fades, sentences shrink, and formal writing thins out.

poles.label: A new register
poles.text: Texting is writing's playground — a new register with its own conventions, and literacy's net effect is more writing, not worse.

hovertip.issue: Are emoji part of language now?

poles.label: A paralanguage
poles.text: Emoji do the work gesture and tone do in speech — they are the body's return to text.

poles.label: Decoration
poles.text: They are punctuation with pictures: expressive, useful, and no more a language than a shrug is a sentence.

hovertip.issue: Is the highest virtue of prose transparent windowpane clarity, or musical density and metaphor?

poles.label: Orwellian Plain Clarity
text: Orwellian Plain Clarity
Concrete nouns and active verbs prevent intellectual dishonesty and make complex ideas immediately testable.

poles.label: Baroque Rhythmic Ornament
text: Baroque Rhythmic Ornament
Cadence, ambiguity, and rich imagery carry emotional truths that flat prose strips away.

categories.name: Words in motion
categories.about: How meanings drift, new words are born, and old words become weapons or wounds.

hovertip.issue: 'Literally' now means its opposite; 'decimate' lost its ten. Is drift decay or life?

poles.label: Trust the drift
poles.text: Drift is the language metabolizing experience; every word you love arrived by it.

poles.label: Hold the line
poles.text: When a word slides, a distinction dies with it; somebody should hold the line on the useful ones.

hovertip.issue: How fast should new words be welcomed into dictionaries and formal prose?

poles.label: Adopt early
poles.text: A dictionary that waits a decade is a history book; record the word when the culture starts using it.

poles.label: Make them earn it
poles.text: Most coinages are foam; a word should survive its season before it is crowned.

hovertip.issue: Does a taboo word's moral weight depend on speaker intent, or do certain words carry harm regardless of context?

poles.label: Context & Intent Rule
text: Context & Intent Rule
Treating quotation, irony, and reclamation identically to malice flattens moral judgment.

poles.label: Inherent Lexical Harm
text: Inherent Lexical Harm
Certain words carry accumulated historical violence that wounds listeners regardless of benign intent.

hovertip.issue: Can conscious social advocacy legitimately reshape pronouns and vocabulary, or should change stay strictly organic?

poles.label: Organic Bottom-Up Drift
text: Organic Bottom-Up Drift
Top-down pronoun and term mandates feel unnatural and provoke backlash against the very goals they seek.

poles.label: Intentional Inclusive Reform
text: Intentional Inclusive Reform
Language has always been shaped by conscious civic choices, and updating terms reduces real exclusion.

hovertip.issue: Does a word's origin tell you what it really means?

poles.label: The true meaning
poles.text: Origins are roots: knowing them disciplines usage and rescues distinctions the present has blurred.

poles.label: A good story
poles.text: Etymology is biography, not destiny — 'nice' once meant ignorant, and nobody owes the past their meaning.

categories.name: Learning & machines
categories.about: How languages are learned and taught, and what happens when machines join the conversation.

hovertip.issue: What is the honest way to learn a language?

poles.label: Immersion
poles.text: Drown usefully: comprehension under pressure wires the language in the way childhood did.

poles.label: Grammar first
poles.text: Adults are not children; explicit grammar is the shortcut their analytic minds are for.

poles.label: Both, in turn
poles.text: Immersion for fluency, grammar for accuracy — sequenced, each covers the other's blind spot.

hovertip.issue: Is there a childhood window after which native-like fluency closes?

poles.label: A real window
poles.text: Accent, at least, is set early; late learners can master everything except sounding born there.

poles.label: A soft slope
poles.text: Motivation and hours explain most of the gap; the 'window' is mostly a slope of circumstance.

hovertip.issue: Should a literary translation feel like smooth native prose, or retain the strange texture of the source language?

poles.label: Foreignizing Fidelity
text: Foreignizing Fidelity
Preserving unfamiliar idioms stretches the reader's mind toward the original culture's actual rhythm.

poles.label: Domesticating Fluency
text: Domesticating Fluency
A great translation recreates the living emotional impact the original had on its first readers.

hovertip.issue: Machine translation is now instant and free. What changes?

poles.label: Good enough
poles.text: The practical language barrier is over; what remains is polish, and polish was always the smaller half.

poles.label: A flattening
poles.text: Machines translate the average of their training: idiom, register, and the brave choice all flatten toward the mean.

hovertip.issue: How sharply does human language stand apart from animal communication and large language models?

poles.label: Continuity With Animal Signals
text: Continuity With Animal Signals
Whale songs, bird syntax, and primate calls show evolutionary roots rather than an absolute chasm.

poles.label: Genuine Understanding in LLMs
text: Genuine Understanding in LLMs
Mastering distributional semantics across trillions of words captures real structural meaning, not empty mimicry.

hovertip.issue: Are sign languages languages in the full sense?

poles.label: Full languages
poles.text: They have grammar, poetry, slang, and dialects — everything but sound; the question answers itself.

poles.label: A different kind
poles.text: They are full communication systems whose visual grammar works so differently that 'language' stretches to cover them.

ecologist.name: The Linguistic Ecologist
ecologist.about: Views every dialect and endangered tongue as an irreplaceable storehouse of human perception and cultural memory.

payload.aboutMe: Views every dialect and endangered tongue as an irreplaceable storehouse of human perception and cultural memory.

stylist.name: The Classical Stylist
stylist.about: Loves precision, historical continuity, and transparent prose that keeps shared civic and literary conversation sharp across generations.

payload.aboutMe: Loves precision, historical continuity, and transparent prose that keeps shared civic and literary conversation sharp across generations.

pragmatist.name: The Cognitive Pragmatist
pragmatist.about: Approaches language as an adaptive, evolving tool shaped by human brains, usage, and technology rather than sacred rules.

payload.aboutMe: Approaches language as an adaptive, evolving tool shaped by human brains, usage, and technology rather than sacred rules.

lingua-nativist.name: Chomskyan Generative Nativist
lingua-nativist.about: The Chomskyan Generative Nativist holds that Universal Grammar is an innate biological faculty: children acquire language not by imitation or general learning but because the human brain comes equipped with the structure of possible grammars. Chomsky (1957) founded generative grammar in Syntactic Structures and (1965) stated the nativist programme in Aspects of the Theory of Syntax — the poverty of the stimulus means the knowledge must already be in the child.

payload.aboutMe: Universal Grammar is an innate biological faculty: children grow language the way they grow arms, because the structure is already in the brain — Chomsky.

explicitness.help: Depth 1 (Overview) is a light survey of the recorded stances. Depth 5 (Dissertation defense) is full scholarly rigor: steelman each stance, raise the strongest objections, and answer them.

prompt.opening: Write an informed discussion between the stances recorded on this map.
rules: Present each recorded stance fairly and in its strongest form — steelman, don't strawman.
Show where the stances agree, where they part, and what follows from each position.
Use the recorded ratings as emphasis: 80–100 central, 56–79 strong support, 36–55 lighter, and 0–35 optional curiosity.
Use only the named topics below. Do not add, imply, or reference any unlisted stance.
Do not invent positions, sources, or facts beyond the supplied data.
prompt.rigor: At maximum depth, length, and rigor, write at dissertation-defense standard: state each position precisely, raise the strongest objections to each, answer them, and defend the conclusion against a skeptical examiner.

phases.help: Enabled phases are added to the generated prompt as a Discussion structure section, in opening, development, closing order. Turn a phase off to leave it out.

groundRules: Present each recorded stance fairly and in its strongest form — steelman, don't strawman.
Speak from your own recorded stance; don't speak for the other side.
Take turns: one position at a time, each side heard fully before replies.
Objections go to the position, not the person holding it.
Anyone may call a pause; the discussion resumes only when everyone is ready.
What the profiles agree on is common ground — start there, and return to it when the discussion stalls.

prompt.opening: Write a moderated discussion plan for the stances recorded on this map.
rules: Present each recorded stance fairly and in its strongest form — steelman, don't strawman.
Show where the stances agree, where they part, and what follows from each position.
Use the recorded ratings as emphasis: 80–100 central, 56–79 strong support, 36–55 lighter, and 0–35 optional curiosity.
Structure the plan in Opening, Development, and Closing, with timed segments and a check-in between segments.
Give each side its strongest form before comparing them; never let one side speak for the other.
Use only the named topics below. Do not add, imply, or reference any unlisted stance.
Do not invent positions, sources, or facts beyond the supplied data.
